transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Amir Patel (Redwood AE), Sofia Nguyen (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Head of ML - LexiHealth), Maria Gomez (Infra Engineer - LexiHealth), Eli Turner (CTO - LexiHealth)

Summary (auto): scoping POC to validate throughput/latency and integration with customer's existing load harness. Focus on comparing streaming vs non-streaming and verifying KV/prefix caching behavior with customer prompts.

Transcript:
[00:00] Amir (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro, i'm amir from Redwood, with sofia our se, and we wanted to run through the benchmark plan and how we'll integrate with your harness.
[00:10] Daniel (LexiHealth): thanks, yeah, appreciate it. we're really trying to validate perf before we commit to dedicated. main ask is we need to see stream latency and overall cost numbers.
[00:18] Maria (LexiHealth): hi all, i'm marIA infra, i'll own the scripts and the k8s side for us.
[00:24] Sofia (Redwood SE): awesome, thanks marIa, and eli?
[00:27] Eli (LexiHealth): hey folks, eli here, i'll be overall sponsor, interested in the timeline more than the gory details.
[00:33] Amir: quick agenda: 1) confirm success criteria 2) workload sizing and canonical scripts 3) streaming vs non-streaming behavior and how we run the harness 4) infra and security notes 5) next steps. sound good?
[00:40] Daniel: yep

[02:05] Sofia: to start success criteria, what would you say are your measurable targets? latency p95/token, throughput, and cost are common.
[02:12] Daniel: top-level: we have an interactive product so perceived latency is important. target is p95 end-to-end for streaming first token under 250ms ideally 200ms. throughput-wise our peak is about 40 concurrent users, typical request distribution is bursts up to 120 rps with short sequences (avg 120 tokens) and some long ones (up to 1k tokens) for history.
[02:36] Amir: good detail — cost target?
[02:38] Eli: we have budget constraints: looking for < $0.06 per 1k tokens at scale is our ballpark else we need to faff with quantization heavier.
[02:46] Maria: and security: SOC2 plus KMS/HSM integration, logs retained for 90 days, and we need audit logs for model usage.

[05:00] Sofia: noted. For the harness, do you already have load scripts? is it an internal JMeter/locust harness or do you use k6?
[05:10] Maria: we use an in-house harness based on locust, but we can export canonical request scripts, python snippets, and a k6 YAML. we'll also record realistic prompt sets.
[05:18] Amir: perfect. how do you currently call models? streaming websocket style or synchronous REST?
[05:22] Daniel: primary is websockets streaming for chat, but we also have some sync batch inference for nightly jobs. so we'll want both tested.

[07:15] Sofia: ok so integration plan: best practice is we run two passes: 1) non-streaming synchronous tests to measure raw throughput and peak token/s with batching and 2) streaming tests to measure time-to-first-token and p95 token latency under realistic concurrency. we'll run each with your scripts so results are comparable.
[07:33] Amir: we typically provision a dedicated test pool that matches expected production (e.g., 8x A100 equiv or 4x H100 depending on quant) and run the harness. we'll share the harness runbook + spreadsheet.
[07:45] Maria: 8x A100 is fine for initial, we can do H100 later. question: how do you simulate prefix/KV cache warm-ups? a lot of our requests reuse conversation context.
[07:58] Sofia: great point — we support a warm-up phase in the harness where we pre-seed the KV cache by replaying representative dialogs to the same model variant; we can parameterize cache hit rates so you can see delta when cache is cold vs warm.

[09:40] Daniel: and on streaming vs non-streaming what's the usual gap? like do you see much worse throughput for stream?
[09:46] Sofia: streaming has slightly higher overhead per connection because of websocket state, but it reduces perceived latency since first token is delivered earlier. in our tests we've seen non-streaming batch throughput higher by 20-30% for pure tokens/s, but streaming gives better p95 for interactive. depends on your SLO.
[10:05] Amir: also quantization profile matters. 4-bit quant gives more tokens/s but sometimes small quality regressions; we can include one run with the quantized model if you want.
[10:13] Eli: yes please include a quantized run, we want to measure quality vs cost trade.

[12:00] Sofia: one integration detail: if you're running in VPC/private, we'll need either an SSH tunnel for the on-prem harness to reach Redwood test endpoints or you can push scripts to an isolated test runner in your VPC. which do you prefer?
[12:14] Maria: we prefer the harness run inside our VPC to avoid egress, we can spin up an ec2 runner and provide a peered route, or we can give you short-lived keys and you run externally. we'll aim for in-VPC run.
[12:26] Amir: good — we'll provide a VPC runbook and a temporary token option if needed.

[14:20] Daniel: about metrics, we want token-level latency and per-route costs plus tail latencies, and an exportable CSV.
[14:29] Amir: the benchmark spreadsheet includes per-run breakdown: tokens generated, avg token latency, p50/p90/p95 token latency, cost estimate, GPU utilization, and payload sizes. we'll add a specific column for stream time-to-first-byte.

[16:00] Maria: any pitfalls you've seen when customers reuse their own scripts? sometimes our harness has rate limiters or retry logic that skews results.
[16:09] Sofia: yes common — we'll review the scripts before running and recommend small edits: remove client-side retries, ensure deterministic inter-arrival times, and make sure you seed caches intentionally. also disable local batching logic in client during the non-streaming run.

[18:30] Daniel: timeline — how long for initial run to get numbers we can look at?
[18:36] Amir: if we get scripts + prompts by Nov 4, we can run a baseline non-streaming by Nov 6 and streaming by Nov 9, deliver spreadsheet by Nov 10. this fits your timeline?
[18:46] Eli: yes that works, fast enough for exec review.

[20:05] Maria: security — for SOC2 and KMS, do you support customer-managed keys in the private deployment?
[20:12] Amir: yes for Private deployments we support customer KMS/HSM integration. for Hosted we have envelope encryption and can integrate with customer-managed KMS for dedicated customers depending on contract. we'll share the security pack.
[20:25] Daniel: audit logs retention — we need 90 days, and ability to export usage by user.
[20:30] Sofia: we can produce token-level usage logs and map tokens to API keys, and we can set retention windows. we'll include that in the security doc bundle.

[22:10] Maria: can you also produce a run where we measure cold-start for model variants? sometimes model swap causes lag.
[22:18] Sofia: absolutely — harness supports a scenario with model swap and measures cold-start time to steady-state. we'll capture image pull / model load time where applicable.

[24:00] Daniel: ok, success criteria for us to sign off on POC: 1) streaming p95 time-to-first-token < 250ms for 90% of runs at peak 120 rps 2) cost below $0.06 per 1k tokens or clear path to that with quantization 3) no security blockers (SOC2 docs + KMS) 4) quality measured by our rubric (we'll provide).
[24:28] Amir: good to have these codified. we'll add them to the spreadsheet as pass/fail columns.

[26:00] Sofia: operationally the harness will run three stages: warm-up (cache seeding), steady-state non-streaming, steady-state streaming. each steady-state will be 10-20 minutes to get stable tail metrics.
[26:15] Maria: 10 minutes might be short for long-tail metrics, can you do 20?
[26:20] Sofia: yes we can set 20 minutes per run if you prefer.

[28:10] Daniel: how do you measure quality? our rubric has hallucination rate and factual accuracy on a set of prompts; do you run evals in parallel?
[28:20] Amir: we can run a small eval harness in parallel or post-run. typically we run a quality pass against your labeled prompts and return exact-match/F1/hallucination counts. we won't run full-scale evals in the high-throughput run to avoid conflating metrics.

[30:05] Maria: is there anything special we need to change in our Locust scripts for streaming?
[30:12] Sofia: for streaming you want to emulate persistent connections and measure time-to-first-token per connection. Locust has websocket clients; we can share a canonical implementation. ensure you don't reconnect per token or you'll skew metrics.

[32:00] Daniel: question on batching — do you do server-side continuous batching for sync calls? and can we configure batch sizes?
[32:08] Sofia: our runtime does continuous batching and adaptive batch sizing; for the benchmark we can fix batch sizes or leave adaptive. we'll provide runs for both adaptive and fixed (e.g. batch=8, batch=16).

[34:20] Eli: what about model variants? we'll probably test two: a high-quality 70B variant and a quantized 13B for cost comparison.
[34:28] Amir: that's common. we'll include both in the run matrix and label runs clearly.

[36:00] Maria: any known issues with streaming over peered VPC? we've seen websocket timeouts if ALB idle timeout is low.
[36:08] Sofia: yes watch the load balancer idle timeout and connection management — we recommend a 15-30 minute idle. also health checks and max-connections limits on the runner matter. we'll include a VPC checklist.

[38:05] Daniel: can you provide examples of past runs so we can sanity check numbers?
[38:11] Amir: yes i'll redact customer names but share two redacted runs: one streaming-heavy retail chat and one non-streaming batch summarization. you'll see the token/s and p95 numbers.

[40:00] Maria: on metrics export format, CSV is fine but also give a JSON with per-token times if possible.
[40:07] Sofia: we can provide both CSV and a JSONL trace for one representative run.

[42:05] Daniel: for acceptance, after you run the harness and deliver spreadsheet we will run an internal review and then sign off or request a follow-up test.
[42:12] Eli: and we'll want a short exec summary for the board.

[44:00] Amir: recap of action items: amir to share benchmark spreadsheet and sample runs; sofia to prepare dedicated config and VPC runbook; marIa to upload scripts and prompt sets; daniel to confirm success rubric. we'll aim to have first non-streaming baseline by nov 6.
[44:18] Maria: confirmed.
[44:22] Daniel: one more thing: can you measure GPU utilization and memory pressure during runs? we need realistic BOM sizing for dedicated.
[44:30] Sofia: yes we'll capture GPU util, VRAM, and estimate concurrency per GPU. add that to the spreadsheet.

[46:50] Amir: any risks? the main ones are script mismatch and client-side retries. if we notice retries we'll pause and collaborate on remediation. also long token requests can blow up tail latency; we'll flag and send recommendations (prefix caching, chunking).
[47:10] Daniel: understood.

[49:00] Maria: does your harness simulate flaky network? we want to see behavior under jitter.
[49:07] Sofia: we can add a run with injected latency/jitter, but it's optional. we usually do a normal run first then a resilience run.

[50:30] Amir: OK wrapping up — i'll email the spreadsheet + runbook and create a shared folder. final Qs?
[50:38] Eli: none from me, thanks.
[50:42] Daniel: thanks everyone.
[50:45] Amir: thanks, we'll follow up with dates and deliverables.

End meeting.
